messages:
laura_support: Heads up — acme-prod (tenant: acme) on dedicated-nyc-1 is returning a lot of 429s and p95 latency has jumped. Customer says their summarize-long-context endpoint started failing ~02:30 UTC. Can we triage urgently?

mark_infra: On it. Any quick repro or logs?

laura_support: Repro snippet from customer:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \ 
 -d '{"model":"gpt-16k-long","input":"<~120k token doc>"}'
```
Response: `429 Throttled: kv_cache_pressure`
And from router logs: `kv_evictions=1834 evict_rate=310/s kv_fragmentation=0.68 mem_free=320MB`

sara_oncall: Looking at metrics for nyc-1 — KV cache resident dropped 72% -> 18% between 02:27-02:33. Evictions/sec spike correlates with a burst of very long-context requests from tenant acme. Autoscaler did not add capacity: observed scale cooldown + pending GPU allocation delay (~120s).

eli_sre: That fragmentation number (0.68) + mem_free that low screams long-context blowouts — KV windows per worker are huge so coalesced free space is low. Noisy neighbor behavior: one tenant's longctx requests are causing repeated full-window evictions.

laura_support: Customer also says retries increased their bill unexpectedly and they're asking for credit. Paul, FYI.

paul_cust_success: I've already pinged acme. They're requesting ETA and a temporary mitigation. They want traffic unblocked — high priority.

mark_infra: Quick mitigations we can try now:
1) tenant-level throttle: cap max_context_tokens for acme to 65k (prevents >100k blasts)
2) increase kv_reservation for acme to 12% so they keep a minimum cache footprint
3) pin acme to fallback model `gpt-8k-fallback` that bypasses large-KV paths
Which should we apply first?

laura_support: Apply throttle + pin fallback first, then kv_reservation if still noisy. Customer prefers a soft cap rather than full block.

infra-bot: Incident created INC-2026-033 | Title: KV pressure in nyc-1 | Severity: S2 | Owners: eng-runtime, infra.

eli_sre: Repro steps for infra to validate:
1) run this load generator from staging into dedicated-nyc-1 under a test tenant:
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do \
  ./load-gen --model gpt-16k-long --prompt-file big_doc.txt --concurrency 8 &
done
```
2) watch `/metrics` for `kv_evictions`, `kv_fragmentation`, `mem_free`
We see evict_rate -> 200-400/s and fragmentation jump in ~3-5m.

sara_oncall: Also note autoscaler logs: `scale_request rejected: backoff-active` — autoscale cooldown prevented a new replica during the first wave. We'll look at shortening cooldown for dedicated-nyc-1 as a follow-up but can't change that mid-incident without risk.

mark_infra: I patched tenant throttle (max_context_tokens=65536) and pinned acme to gpt-8k-fallback. Rolling now.

laura_support: Update: customer traffic dropped errors to near-zero after pinning. Still watching KV metrics.

paul_cust_success: Confirmed with customer — errors stopped, they accepted temporary cap. Asking for credit and postmortem.

ops_manager: Requesting a short postmortem: owner eng-runtime, include root cause (tenant long-context + autoscale cooldown + KV fragmentation) and remediation (throttles, reservation, autoscale cooldown tuning, tenant fair-share). Target ETA: 48h.

eli_sre: Next steps I recommend:
- run defrag job on workers in maintenance window (low-risk)
- add tenant reservation feature flag default = 3% and allow on-demand bump
- evaluate autoscale cooldown heuristics to be workload-aware

laura_support: Thanks all. I'll update the ticket with the actions and the customer-facing message. :thumbsup:
